body:
I think changing behavior is too much of a risk for existing projects.

It might be better to introduce a new property `random_pitch_semitones` that acts as a log-scale view of `random_pitch`. We could add to the documentation the gotcha that direct use of `random_pitch` is discouraged because it will non-uniformly randomize the audible frequency.

Appreciate the suggestions @Ivorforce ! I've updated the branch considering your idea of keeping `random_pitch` under the hood.

Now, in the editor inspector, the `random_pitch` slider has been replaced with a `random_pitch_semitones` slider, but it still saves and loads the value as the original `random_pitch`, so this shouldn't break compatibility. I would love it if a couple other people could take a look and/or test that out to be certain.

Some nitpick thoughts, curious what others think:

- It is technically possible to fix the higher-pitch random bias without random_pitch_semitones, but IMO using a multiplier to define a random pitch range is strange, and using semitones makes a lot more sense.
- We could have two parameters, one for a multiplier and one for semitones, and they could be combined when doing random pitch calculations. That being said, it may feel strange having two visible parameters that essentially do the same thing, just on a different scale.
- `random_pitch_semitones` is descriptive, but doesn't match the style of the other property `random_volume_offset_db`. `random_pitch_offset_semitones` is more descriptive, but is a bit long.
- Currently, the conversion from a frequency ratio to semitones happens all inside the functions where they're needed. It could be useful to add a function `semitones_to_freq_ratio` and vice-versa in the math functions, though I imagine that would be a separate PR. If that would be desired, I could take care of that, and update this PR if that's merged.

A bit of a confession: I'm still pretty new to any programming language that isn't GDScript, and I'm still wrapping my head around Godot's architecture. The fact that loading `random_pitch` into `random_pitch_semitones` works when opening an asset is a bit of a mystery to me. I couldn't tell you exactly what's happening. I'd love if someone looked at that and checked if I did that right.

This looks great!
Notably, this means the PR still changes behavior, but in an arguably perfectly favorable way. Personally, I think it's a 'breaking change' that's defendable to be merged in a minor version.

> Some nitpick thoughts, curious what others think:
> 
> * It is technically possible to fix the higher-pitch random bias without random_pitch_semitones, but IMO using a multiplier to define a random pitch range is strange, and using semitones makes a lot more sense.

Agreed.

> * We could have two parameters, one for a multiplier and one for semitones, and they could be combined when doing random pitch calculations. That being said, it may feel strange having two visible parameters that essentially do the same thing, just on a different scale.

If `random_pitch` did the same calculation as before, it wouldn't be the _exact_ same as using `random_pitch` would be perfectly backwards compatible (and probably deprecated).
I would prefer what you did, but if other people are concerned about the behavior change, it's an alternative worth considering.

> * `random_pitch_semitones` is descriptive, but doesn't match the style of the other property `random_volume_offset_db`. `random_pitch_offset_semitones` is more descriptive, but is a bit long.

I think `random_pitch_semitones` is fine.

> * Currently, the conversion from a frequency ratio to semitones happens all inside the functions where they're needed. It could be useful to add a function `semitones_to_freq_ratio` and vice-versa in the math functions, though I imagine that would be a separate PR. If that would be desired, I could take care of that, and update this PR if that's merged.

I don't think that's needed as frequency ratios aren't all that useful practically.
From the principle of minimality, Godot tries to avoid creating new functions until needed. I think it's fine to keep the conversions where you put them, until they're actually needed elsewhere.

> A bit of a confession: I'm still pretty new to any programming language that isn't GDScript, and I'm still wrapping my head around Godot's architecture. The fact that loading `random_pitch` into `random_pitch_semitones` works when opening an asset is a bit of a mystery to me. I couldn't tell you exactly what's happening. I'd love if someone looked at that and checked if I did that right.

If this is really some of your earliest non GDScript code, this is an impressive contribution!
Pushed an update with the above suggestions. I really appreciate all your thorough input @Ivorforce , it has helped a ton!
Oh looks like I did miss your last comment! I'll go ahead and pop that in

Discussed during the audio meeting of 2025-06-24. There's in fact two elements in the same PR: a new feature that introduces semitones, and there's the random perception fix.

I think we could easily merge the fix for 4.5, and see afterwards what can be done to make usability better.

Could you split your PR in two, and make this one the fix only?

Appreciate the feedback! Closing this PR now :)
